subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make previously allowlisted or auto-reviewed gateway/daemon lifecycle commands require explicit approval in every non-yolo exec configuration?
rationale: The proposed behavior changes the operational approval contract for existing automated lifecycle workflows and chooses a yolo-mode exception; maintainers must own that security and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Confirm the explicit-approval boundary
options.body: Accept the non-yolo lifecycle restriction, require final-head runtime proof for blocked, yolo, and read-only cases, then proceed with normal merge review.

options.title: Preserve prior automation by policy
options.body: Retain the existing allowlist or auto-review behavior for a documented subset of lifecycle operations and narrow the classifier accordingly.

options.title: Pause for a broader approval-policy design
options.body: Defer this large taxonomy until maintainers define a stable shared command-classification ownership model.

recommendation.title: Confirm the explicit-approval boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the non-yolo lifecycle restriction, require final-head runtime proof for blocked, yolo, and read-only cases, then proceed with normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level exec-security policy and compatibility decision rather than a contributor-only repair detail.
